mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay near their current depressed levels for another month, weekday shopping traffic will remain weak and RETAIL_REC will stay below its prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above its last-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain within 5 points of their current levels for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below its already weak baseline will reduce spontaneous mall and dining trips within one week, pushing RETAIL_REC lower relative to the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 and stays there for one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next 7 days after TRANSIT crosses below -30, or retail mobility rises despite sustained transit weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility holds above its recent level while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, household errand clustering substitutes for discretionary shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and GROCERY_PHARM remains above 20 for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility signals weather- or holiday-driven outdoor activity that diverts time away from indoor retail destinations, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points from its current weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior four-week average after PARKS increases by at least 8 points from the current level.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES recover faster than TRANSIT, more commuting will occur by private modes and weekday shopping trips will also improve, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while TRANSIT remains below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after WORKPLACES improves and TRANSIT stays weak, or retail falls despite the commuting rebound.

mechanism_narrative: Under a stable restriction regime, a persistent gap between high RESIDENTIAL time and low TRANSIT use indicates home-centered activity that suppresses discretionary retail visits, so RETAIL_REC remains below the prior four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last four-week average even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and TRANSIT stays depressed for most of the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM after its recent plateau would signal fewer essential-stop trips and less bundled shopping, which should pull RETAIL_REC down within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 20 after staying above 20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after GROCERY_PHARM drops below 20 from an above-20 plateau.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remains very weak while TRANSIT is flat, the city is likely in a demand-suppressed phase rather than a substitution phase, so retail mobility will stay soft over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining below -20 and TRANSIT not improving materially.
